ai.description: The Taiwanese Habu reaches 100–160 cm. It is brown with dark, pale-edged dorsal blotches and a triangular head. Key features include a sharply pointed snout and keeled scales.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Protobothrops mucrosquamatus* is distinguished by its distinct, dark-edged, pale vertebral blotches and a prominent, elongated postocular stripe, features absent in similar Indian pit vipers.
ai.habitat: The Taiwanese Habu inhabits subtropical forests, bamboo groves, and agricultural areas, typically ranging from lowlands up to elevations of approximately 2,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Taiwanese Habu is primarily nocturnal, often remaining motionless for hours as an ambush predator while waiting for small mammals or frogs to pass within striking range.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Protobothrops mucrosquamatus* is oviparous, laying clutches of 5–23 eggs. Breeding typically occurs in spring, with hatching observed during the summer months.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Protobothrops mucrosquamatus* occurs in Northeast India (Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Mizoram) at elevations ranging from 200 to 2,000 meters in the Eastern Himalayas.
